why: The student reads the semicolon after if (x > 0) in its everyday sense, as just ending the line, so they think the println is the if's body. In Java that ; is an empty statement and is the whole then branch, so "positive" is always printed, as the run output shows.

concepts.why: The mistake is about what makes up the if's body, which belongs to the empty statement, not about how an if works.

concepts.quote: positive is not printed, because x > 0 is false.
concepts.why: This is the SemicolonAfterIfHeader error: the student ignores that the ; ends the if, so the println always runs.
